title: M3Care: Learning with Missing Modalities in Multimodal Healthcare Data

problem.claim: Missing modalities are common in real-world clinical scenarios involving multimodal EHR data, while conventional methods assume all modalities are available for every patient.

gap.claim: Existing approaches mostly rely on generative mappings from latent space to input space, which the authors characterize as an unstable ill-posed inverse problem.

contributions.claim: M3Care is an end-to-end model that compensates for missing patient modalities to support clinical analysis.
The model imputes task-related latent information using auxiliary information from similar neighbors selected by a task-guided modality-adaptive similarity metric.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show that M3Care outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report that M3Care's discovered findings are consistent with experts and medical knowledge and may provide useful insights and explanations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal EHR data are used in clinical applications, but complete modality availability is an unrealistic assumption in practice.
Existing generative approaches are framed as unstable ill-posed inverse problems.
M3Care addresses missing modalities through direct learning, latent task-related imputation, and clinical task execution.
A task-guided modality-adaptive similarity metric identifies patients with matching uncensored modalities and uses similar neighbors as auxiliary information.
The authors report stronger performance than state-of-the-art baselines and consistency with expert and medical knowledge.

source_observation.claim: The method imputes task-related latent information rather than reconstructing raw missing modalities.

interpretation.claim: When raw-data recovery is unstable or unnecessary, task-specific latent compensation may provide a more direct modeling target.

application.claim: For incomplete multimodal prediction tasks, consider optimizing missing information for downstream task utility instead of full modality reconstruction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that latent task-related imputation is preferable for tasks requiring faithful recovery of raw missing data.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, clinical tasks, baseline results, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, or missingness conditions.
